intro: Picture this: you finish work or check in to a room with its own kitchen, like a private condo, then in the evening you head up to soak in a 25-metre infinity pool watching the sun set over the Gulf of Thailand, before topping it off with a drink at the rooftop bar on the very top floor — Oakwood Hotel & Residence Sri Racha is a 5-star hotel and serviced apartment under the Oakwood (Ascott) brand, sitting in central Si Racha, Si Racha District, Chonburi, right on Sri Racha Nakorn 3 Road · what most people talk about is the fully equipped in-room kitchens plus the sea-view infinity pool and the Atara rooftop bar that make it comfortable for both a single night and a long monthly stay · there are 458 units from Studio to Two Bedroom, starting at around ฿1,800/night, rated 9.3 from 642 reviews on Trip.com, with Tripadvisor ranking it #2 among hotels in Si Racha

body.html: Overview and who it suits — to put it as simply as possible, Oakwood Hotel & Residence Sri Racha is a place for people who want "the feel of home in a luxury serviced apartment" in central Si Racha, rather than a beachfront holiday resort like Bang Saen or Pattaya · it's a 5-star hotel and serviced apartment under the Oakwood brand from the Ascott group, open since 2017, on Sri Racha Nakorn 3 Road in central Si Racha, Si Racha District, Chonburi · with 458 units that all have in-room kitchens and a concept built for both short stays and long monthly stays, real reviews consistently say the people who suit it best are those coming to work or run errands around Laem Chabang, the industrial estates and the port — engineers, staff at foreign companies, and people posted here long-term — because there's a kitchen to cook in and full facilities just like living in a condo · another group that says they were impressed is families and couples who want a spacious room with a kitchen, use the sea-view infinity pool and the rooftop bar, plus people who travel to Si Racha on business and want a central stay within walking distance of malls and restaurants · on the flip side, anyone set on staying right by the beach to swim in the sea in front of the property may feel this is more of a downtown high-rise than a beachfront resort, and should consider somewhere around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · in short, Oakwood plays on "living comfortably like home in the middle of town" with five-star facilities, rather than selling the image of a resort where you can step straight down to the sea

Location and getting around — this is one of Oakwood's top selling points, scoring as high as around 9.6 out of 10 for location in real reviews · the hotel sits on Sri Racha Nakorn 3 Road in central Si Racha, a district surrounded by malls, restaurants and markets · reviews often mention that it's about a 9-minute walk to Robinson Lifestyle Sriracha, and it's close to the Ko Loi pier, the town's seaside landmark, plus Si Racha's well-known markets and seafood restaurants · for getting further afield, the hotel is close to Laem Chabang port and the industrial-estate area, which is the main reason workers choose to stay here · Si Racha train station is about 3–4 km away, and the Sri Racha Glass Sky Bridge is about 12 km away · for airports, it's about a 40 min drive from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and about an 80 min drive from Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK), and the hotel offers a paid shuttle you can ask about · one thing worth saying straight is that even though it's central and within walking distance of a mall, getting to other spots in Chonburi or Pattaya is still easiest with your own car, because public transport in Si Racha isn't as dense as in bigger cities — the upside is that the hotel has free parking

"The room is huge, with a full kitchen like a private condo — perfect for working in Laem Chabang on a long stay · the sea-view infinity pool is gorgeous in the evening, and you can easily walk to Robinson, you just need a car if you want to go further."

Room types and decor — Oakwood has 458 rooms and serviced apartments in total, split into several tiers to handle both one-night guests and long-term monthly stays · it starts with the Studio Deluxe King at around 33 sqm, which is the entry room but still has a small in-room kitchen and is roomier than a standard room at most hotels · stepping up is the Studio Executive at around 51 sqm and the one-bedroom group such as the One Bedroom Deluxe and One Bedroom Premium Sea View at around 56 sqm, which have a separate living room and, in some rooms, a sea view · the largest are the Two Bedroom Deluxe at around 91 sqm and the Two Bedroom Executive at around 109 sqm for families or groups who want plenty of space · what sets Oakwood apart from a regular hotel is that every room has a fully equipped in-room kitchen, a private balcony, a sitting area, and a washing machine in some room types, so you can live just like you're at home · a detail many international reviewers especially like is the Japanese-style auto-clean toilet in the bathroom, a small touch that leaves an impression · the decor is a clean, easy-on-the-eyes modern style in warm tones, focused on real usability over flashiness · most real reviews agree the rooms are clean, very spacious, with comfortable beds, and quiet, and the room size in particular comes up again and again · if you want a sea view, ask for a Sea View room when you book, because not every room faces the sea, and higher floors get a wider view of the Gulf of Thailand

Facilities, the pool and the rooftop bar — the most talked-about highlight at Oakwood is the 25-metre infinity pool on level 5 that looks out over the Gulf of Thailand · evening into night is the popular time for guests to head up to soak, take photos, and watch the sun set over the sea · there's a separate children's pool partitioned off, around 50–90 centimetres deep, which puts families with young kids more at ease · besides the pool there's a 24-hour gym with full equipment, a sauna, a jacuzzi and a steam room for anyone who wants to unwind after work or get in a workout · extra spots many people like are the karaoke room, the pool table (billiards), the kids' club and a small library, along with a children's play area · another highlight that photographs well is Atara Sky Bar & Bistro, a rooftop bar on the building's top floor with panoramic Gulf of Thailand views, great for an evening drink · there's also free Wi-Fi everywhere, free parking, a concierge service, and a 24-hour front desk · to be honest, the facilities here are genuinely complete and have a good atmosphere for a five-star serviced apartment, even if the pool leans more toward soaking and taking in the view than serious lap swimming in a large lap pool

Food and restaurants — Oakwood has two main restaurants that handle breakfast and other meals · the main one is trEat Restaurant, all-day dining, serving Thai and international food and acting as the buffet-breakfast venue · many reviews praise the breakfast for its variety and fresh ingredients, with Thai, Asian and Western options, which is a point that earns consistent praise · another spot selling the atmosphere is Atara Sky Bar & Bistro on the rooftop, serving fusion food and drinks with evening Gulf of Thailand views, good for a relaxed dinner or sitting with a drink and the view · a big advantage of staying here is that every room has its own kitchen, so long-stay guests can cook for themselves — economical and convenient for everyday living · combined with the central location within walking distance of Robinson and the surrounding restaurants, many people mix cooking in the room, eating at the hotel, and heading out to try Si Racha's famous seafood restaurants · overall the food at Oakwood is done well and flexibly, suiting both those who want to eat in the hotel and those who want to use the place as a base to explore the town's food scene

Service — service is another point that earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews, scoring around 9.2 out of 10 · many say the staff are friendly, polite and helpful, and there are staff who can communicate in English to look after the international guests coming to work around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates · the personal check-in, the 24-hour front desk, and the concierge who helps with calling a car, booking restaurants or recommending places to visit leave many guests feeling well looked after, especially long-term residents the staff start to recognise · but to be straight about it, some reviews say that the team's responsiveness during busy periods when the hotel is full isn't completely consistent, with suggestions to improve how quickly service moves at peak times · overall, service is still a strength here and one of the reasons the review scores sit so high

Voices from real reviews (the good and the bad) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture lines up fairly closely · on the praise side: a central Si Racha location within walking distance of Robinson and close to the sea, very spacious and clean rooms, a full in-room kitchen like a condo that's great for long stays, comfortable beds, a sea-view infinity pool that's lovely in the evening, the Atara rooftop bar with Gulf views, a gym and onsen/sauna to unwind, the Japanese-style auto-clean toilet, a varied breakfast, and friendly staff · on the watch-out side: what comes up is noise from the bar and the buzz of the downtown area on some nights, especially rooms facing the street or on lower floors · next is service responsiveness during busy periods not being consistent, which some reviews suggest improving, the fact that this is a downtown high-rise rather than a resort you can walk straight down to the beach from, which some people wrongly expect, and the point that getting to other spots is easiest with a car · most of these criticisms are things you can manage by choosing your room and setting expectations right, rather than being major problems, since the overall score still sits high at 9.3 and the hotel still holds a top spot in Si Racha

"Loved how clean and spacious the room was, with a kitchen to cook in myself, and the staff were lovely · the only downside was that on Friday night the noise from the bar downstairs carried up to the room a little — next time I'll ask for a higher floor on the sea-view side instead."

Price comparison and value — nightly rates start at around ฿1,800/night for a Studio Deluxe at standard pricing, rising to around ฿2,500–฿3,500 for the Studio Executive and the one-bedroom group, while the large two-bedroom rooms run from several thousand into the low tens of thousands depending on size and season · for long stays, the hotel has monthly rates that are clearly better value than paying nightly, which is the core selling point of a serviced apartment · what makes Oakwood good value is that you get a 5-star serviced apartment with an in-room kitchen, a sea-view infinity pool, a rooftop bar, a 24-hour gym, a sauna, and very spacious rooms at a starting price that isn't high, which is hard to find in Si Racha · compared with hotels of the same level in this area that mostly focus on just a bedroom and breakfast, Oakwood clearly gives more usable space, a kitchen, and leisure facilities · but compared with a beachfront resort around Bang Saen or Pattaya, those win on stepping straight down to the sea and the holiday atmosphere, while Oakwood wins on the feel of home, the in-room kitchen, and the central location that's convenient for workers · in short, if you weigh room size, an in-room kitchen, and good-value long stays heavily, every baht you pay feels well returned, especially for Laem Chabang workers and families

Good to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if a sea view matters to you, state when booking that you want a Sea View room and choose a high floor, because not every room faces the Gulf of Thailand · two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a high floor or a side that doesn't face the street, because the downtown area is lively with bar noise on some nights · three, if you're planning a long stay, ask about monthly rates and pick a room with a kitchen and an in-room washing machine for value and convenience in daily life · four, make the most of the infinity pool and rooftop bar in the evening for the sunset over the sea, and check the opening hours of the pool, gym and sauna in advance · five, if you drive yourself there's free parking, but if you don't have a car, plan for calling a ride to reach spots beyond the town centre · six, during events or activities around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates rooms tend to fill up fast, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Oakwood Hotel & Residence Sri Racha is the best fit for people who want a luxury serviced apartment with an in-room kitchen in central Si Racha, suiting Laem Chabang workers, long-stay guests, and families who want a spacious room · the very spacious and clean rooms, the full in-room kitchen, the Gulf-of-Thailand infinity pool, the Atara rooftop bar, the 24-hour gym, and the location within walking distance of Robinson and close to the sea make it good value, with little competition at the same price in Si Racha · friendly service and a high review score of 9.3 from 642 reviews are the reasons it holds a top spot in town · but to be honest, this is a downtown high-rise, not a resort you can walk straight down to the beach from, there's noise from the downtown area on some nights you should avoid by choosing your room, and service at peak times isn't consistent every time · if you're looking for a place by the sea where you can step straight down for a swim, this may not be the answer, and you should look at options around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · but for a central Si Racha stay with a kitchen, a sea-view pool, and the feel of home at a price you can reach — Oakwood meets that need well, and it's why it's won over workers and long-stay guests in Si Racha for years

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Oakwood Hotel & Residence Sri Racha, Chonburi

faq.q: Where is Oakwood Hotel & Residence Sri Racha · is it easy to get to?
faq.a: The hotel is at Tower A, 222/2 Sri Racha Nakorn 3 Road in central Si Racha, Chonburi · it's about a 9-minute walk to Robinson Si Racha, close to the Ko Loi pier and the Laem Chabang area · Si Racha train station is about 3–4 km away and the Sri Racha Glass Sky Bridge about 12 km away · it's about 40 minutes from U-Tapao Airport and about 80 minutes from Suvarnabhumi · you can walk to a mall, but getting to other spots is easiest with a car, and there's free parking

faq.q: Does Oakwood Sri Racha have in-room kitchens and is it good for long stays?
faq.a: Very much so · it's a serviced apartment where every room has a fully equipped in-room kitchen, a private balcony, and a sitting area, and some rooms have a washing machine · there's everything from a 33 sqm Studio to a 91–109 sqm Two Bedroom · there are monthly rates for long stays, ideal for people working around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates who need to stay a long time with a kitchen to cook for themselves

faq.q: What's the starting price at Oakwood Sri Racha · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿1,800/night for a Studio Deluxe of about 33 sqm at standard pricing · there's a Studio Executive (~51 sqm), a One Bedroom Premium Sea View (~56 sqm), and a Two Bedroom (~91–109 sqm) for families · there are monthly rates for long stays · rooms fill up fast during events around the industrial estates and Laem Chabang, so compare several platforms before you book

faq.q: Does Oakwood Sri Racha have a pool and a rooftop bar?
faq.a: There's a 25-metre infinity pool on level 5 overlooking the Gulf of Thailand, plus a separate children's pool, a standout that many reviews love · there's a 24-hour gym, a sauna, a jacuzzi, a steam room, a karaoke room and a pool table · and there's Atara Sky Bar & Bistro, a rooftop bar on the top floor with panoramic Gulf of Thailand views, good for an evening drink with the view

faq.q: Who does Oakwood Sri Racha suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people working or running errands around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates, long-stay guests, and families who want a spacious room with a kitchen in central Si Racha within walking distance of malls and restaurants · it's not ideal for anyone set on staying right by the beach to swim in the sea in front of the property, because this is a downtown high-rise — for that, look at Bang Saen or Pattaya instead

faq.q: What are noise and service like at Oakwood Sri Racha?
faq.a: Most reviews praise the clean, spacious rooms and friendly service · but some mention noise from the bar and the buzz of the downtown area on some nights, especially rooms facing the street or on lower floors, and service responsiveness during busy periods not being consistent · if you sleep lightly, it's best to ask for a high floor or the sea-view side that doesn't face the street when you book or check in
